header: Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K, 2nd gen 2023 (AFTKM, codename karat), Fire OS 8.1.8.5 (RS8185.3891N, build 0033018557316),
Android 11 (SDK 30), Brazil. The first Fire OS 8 list here: it starts from amazon-fire-tv-stick-lite-2020/ and
amazon-fire-tv-stick-4k-2018/, and every package new in Fire OS 8 was checked with `dumpsys package` before listing.
FIRE OS: DEBLOAT ONLY. Home is com.amazon.tv.launcher/.ui.HomeActivity_vNext (priority 950); launcher/ does not apply.
Apply:   TV_HOST=<stick ip> tools/disable.sh examples/amazon-fire-tv-stick-4k-2023/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<stick ip> tools/restore.sh examples/amazon-fire-tv-stick-4k-2023/debloat.txt com.amazon.tv.launcher
For the whole list, put HANDLERS_ALLOW=1 in front of the Apply line ($env:HANDLERS_ALLOW=1 for disable.ps1). Since
2026-10-23 disable.sh keeps the app that answers VIEW vnd.android.cursor.item/channel, read as the HDMI input
handler, and here that is com.amazon.tv.livetv/.TvChannelsPlayerActivityAlias: a stick has no tuner or HDMI input.
Seen 2026-10-25 on a Fire TV Stick 4K Plus (AFTMA08C15, karat, RS8185.3891N): livetv was the only listed package
the check held back; the Settings handlers (com.amazon.tv.launcher, com.amazon.tv.settings.v2) are not listed.
Everything is DISABLED for user 0, never uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.
ADB on Fire OS 8: Settings > My Fire TV > About > press select 7 times on the device name, back > Developer Options >
ADB Debugging. Port 5555, accept the prompt on the TV (ro.adb.secure=1).
Applied 2026-10-20 in four batches with a screenshot after each, then rebooted: all 57 stayed disabled, Home, Prime
Video, Netflix, Globoplay and Disney+ open, Wi-Fi validates.
Protected on this build (pm disable-user: "Cannot disable a protected package"), so commented out below, the same set
as Fire OS 7 plus the help app: com.amazon.device.metrics, com.amazon.device.logmanager, com.amazon.device.crashmanager,
com.amazon.diode, com.fireos.usagestats.proxy, com.amazon.ftvads.deeplinking, com.amazon.tv.csapp.
Kept on purpose: com.amazon.tv.launcher, com.amazon.firehomestarter, com.amazon.tv.settings.*, com.amazon.venezia and
com.amazon.tigris (Appstore), com.amazon.tv.ime, remote/Bluetooth services, OTA updates (device.software.ota*,
tv.forcedotaupdater.v2), Alexa voice search, Prime Video (com.amazon.firebat, com.amazon.tv.support), casting and
mirroring (cast.sink, dialservice, awvflingreceiver, whisperplay, whisperlink, com.amazon.tv.matter for Matter
casting), Amazon sign-in for apps (com.amazon.tv.ottssocompanionapp, com.amazon.imp), profiles, com.amazon.tv.oobe
(needed for a factory reset), the screensaver, accessibility (com.amazon.logan), notification center.
com.amazon.imp confirmed load-bearing on a second AFTKRT unit (same karat board, Fire OS 8.1.8.5): disabling it
together with shoptv.client, shoptv.firetv.client, media.recommendations, sneakpeek, systemnotices, tv.earlyaccess
and tv.acr left HomeActivity_vNext resumed and the remote fully responsive, but painted nothing -- confirmed black
on the physical TV. Re-enabling just those eight (imp included) fixed it within seconds, no reboot needed; the
other seven were not re-tested standalone, so this list's existing success with them already disabled stands.
Fire OS 8 packages looked at and left alone: com.amazon.adep (package verification / security events),
com.amazon.platform.fdra (package allowlisting), com.amazon.tv.turnstile (PIN sign-in), com.amazon.tv.consents,
com.amazon.ssm / ssmsys (captive portal, error codes), com.amazon.tiramisubootsupport, com.amazon.d3 (has a demo
content provider but also OOBE and provisioning receivers).
What the list cannot remove: the hero banner, the "Patrocinados" (Sponsored) row and the Luna tile in "Your apps"
come from the launcher's own feed. Point the stick's DNS at a blocker for those (Pi-hole, or Private DNS
dns.adguard-dns.com on Android 11). Also turn off Settings > Preferences > Privacy Settings (Device Usage Data,
Collect App Usage Data, Interest-based Ads) and Featured Content autoplay in the menus: those values sync with the
Amazon account, so the menu is the place to change them, not `settings put`.
Prime Video registers only LEANBACK_LAUNCHER, so `monkey -p com.amazon.firebat 1` does nothing; start
com.amazon.firebat/com.amazon.pyrocore.IgnitionActivity with `am start -n` to test it.
Leave the animation scales at 1.0 on this build. At 0.5 (window, transition and animator) every entry in the
side menu (☰: Settings, Appstore, My Stuff...) closes the menu and goes back to Home without opening anything:
NavigationActivity logs "onStop with slideoutState=false, finishing to prevent stuck menu" before the navigation
request is sent. Back at 1.0, Settings opens again with all 57 packages still disabled.
Additional AFTKRT / karat unit: Fire TV Stick 4K Max 2nd gen, Fire OS 8.1.7.4 (RS8174.3648N),
Android 11 / SDK 30, system incremental 0031877644420, boot-image fingerprint incremental 0031877644288,
kernel 5.10.43-android12-9-ge1cb3cb5ad98, armeabi-v7a app userspace. Report updated 2026-10-24.

header: Chromecast with Google TV 4K (2020, device sabrina, product sabrina_prod_stable), 2 GB RAM
Google TV 14 (SDK 34), build UTTC.250917.004 (14193937)
Second unit: Canada, same build, one day of use (2026-10-22). Notes under "Second unit" below.
Apply:   TV_HOST=<ip> tools/disable.sh examples/google-chromecast-gtv-4k/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<ip> tools/restore.sh examples/google-chromecast-gtv-4k/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.
To keep phone casting and the stock home (no new launcher), use debloat-keep-cast.txt in this folder instead.
Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx. No Live TV app and no HDMI inputs (it's a dongle):
leave live_tv_package empty in config.xml.
Known quirks on this firmware:
- ADB on port 5555 is closed (connection refused) until you pair once through Wireless debugging with
the stock adb: Developer options > Wireless debugging > Pair device with pairing code, `adb pair
<ip:pairport> <code>`, `adb connect <ip:connectport>` (`adb mdns services` lists both ports), then
`adb tcpip 5555`. After that tools/tv.py works on 5555
(docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md, "USB debugging never opens port 5555").
- `cmd package set-home-activity com.gathin.tvhome` returns Success but launcherx stays the default.
Disable BOTH com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx and com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith
(setupwraith re-enables launcherx), only after the new launcher is installed.
- WARNING: setupwraith can own a saved Wi-Fi network on this model too, as on the HD. On the second
unit `dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'` named com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith as the
creator of one of its two saved networks; the network it was on when checked was created by
android.uid.system:1000. Android deletes an app's saved networks when the app is disabled, so
disabling setupwraith deletes that network, and if the stick is on it, Wi-Fi and ADB go with it.
Before disabling setupwraith, forget that network and join it again in Settings > Network &
Internet until every cname reads android.uid.system:1000 (the HD list, same build, also removes it
under Wi-Fi > App preferences). tools/disable.sh skips setupwraith while it owns a network, and
FORCE_SETUPWRAITH=1 overrides that (docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md, "The TV drops off Wi-Fi for good").
- Disabling setupwraith also breaks casting from phones, reported on the Chromecast HD on the same
build (#361). The Cast receiver (com.google.android.apps.mediashell) reads its factory device
credentials from a provider inside setupwraith
(com.google.android.libraries.tv.setupwraith.libs.castinfo.CastInfoProvider), so once the wizard
is gone and the device has rebooted, YouTube on the phone answers "Untrusted device ... couldn't
be verified" and the receiver logs "No private key, hence empty signature" every minute. Keeping
the provider while taking Home away does not work: pm disable-user on
setupwraith/.RecoveryActivity is refused with a SecurityException. Either debloat only (keep
launcherx and setupwraith enabled), or re-enable setupwraith after each boot, wait a minute for
"Created singleton instance of ClientAuthSigner" in logcat, then disable it again - the receiver
holds the credentials in memory, so casting works until the next reboot
(docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md, "Casting fails with Untrusted device").
Seen again after a reboot: re-enabling setupwraith brought no ClientAuthSigner line within 3 minutes
and phones did not list the device at all. Restart the receiver while setupwraith is enabled:
pm enable com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith
logcat -c
am crash com.google.android.apps.mediashell
The system starts it again with a new pid, and "Created singleton instance of ClientAuthSigner"
follows within seconds. Check that pid (pidof com.google.android.apps.mediashell) is still the same
30 s later, then: pm disable-user --user 0 com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith
Not am force-stop plus am start-foreground-service: started that way the receiver never calls
startForeground(), Android kills it after 30 s, and the copy that comes back with setupwraith
already off has no credentials (the signer line came from the killed process) (#2615).
- Turning USB debugging off leaves Wireless debugging listening on its own port. Switch both off when
you are done. tools/adb-closed.py checks 5555 unless it is given that port: note the port from
`adb mdns services` first, and check it with tools/adb-closed.py <ip> <port> before the reboot.
- With launcherx disabled the YouTube button on the remote does nothing. It sends BUTTON_3
(keycode 190). Button Mapper only remaps added buttons in its paid Pro version; Key Mapper
(open source, keymapperorg/KeyMapper) does it for free. Play Store lists Key Mapper as incompatible
with this device, so install the -foss APK from its GitHub releases, then over ADB:
pm grant io.github.sds100.keymapper android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS
settings put secure enabled_accessibility_services io.github.sds100.keymapper/io.github.sds100.keymapper.system.accessibility.MyAccessibilityService
Map trigger "Button 3" (short press) to action "Launch app > YouTube". Record the trigger with the
physical remote: keys injected with `input keyevent 190` don't reach Key Mapper, and D-pad presses
made while recording get added to the trigger.
- com.google.android.tvrecommendations and com.google.android.apps.education.cast2class ship
disabled at the factory; `pm disable-user` on them fails with "Shell cannot change component
state". Don't add them to a restore list either.
- Disabling dreamx leaves screensaver_components pointing at it. Point it at the launcher's clock:
settings put secure screensaver_components com.gathin.tvhome/.ClockDream
- Animation scales already ship at 0.5x on this build.
- Disable in small batches, and wait before walking away. A run that disabled 21 packages in one
batch had every one report "new state", then the device rebooted: 19 of the 21 were back
afterwards. PackageManager writes package-restrictions.xml asynchronously, so a package disabled
seconds before a reboot is lost while ones disabled minutes earlier (launcherx, setupwraith)
survive. Four batches of 4/4/4/7 with a 20-second pause after each, checking the device is still
up between them, went through with no reboot.
- If the device does reboot, check the uptime before assuming a crash loop:
GET http://<ip>:8008/setup/eureka_info reports it, and one reboot with a steadily climbing
uptime afterwards is not a loop.
Second unit. The list's telemetry and preloaded-app groups were applied (the screensaver pair and
setupwraith were kept), plus a few apps by choice;
after a reboot the disabled list was unchanged. Private DNS validated, and YouTube and Plex loaded
their profiles. Power and Ethernet came through one USB-C hub.
- On Ethernet the Wireless debugging toggle flipped straight back off: unplug the cable, join Wi-Fi
and pair as above. Wireless debugging also went off at every reboot (Wi-Fi drops during boot) and
had to be switched on again by hand; the pairing was kept and the stock adb reconnected on its own.
Port 5555 from `adb tcpip` lasted until the next reboot.
- The hub stayed powered with USB debugging on: `ip link` still listed eth0 (NO-CARRIER only because
the cable was out), while `dumpsys usb` printed host_connected=false and sys.usb.config was "none",
so host_connected=false was no proof the hub was gone. With USB debugging still on, plugging the
Ethernet cable back in brought the Chromecast up on Ethernet, and tools/adb-closed.py then reported
5555 refused (not checked whether that came from a restart or from Wireless debugging going off).
- The remote ("Chromecast Remote", 18d1:9450; /odm/usr/keylayout/Vendor_18d1_Product_9450.kl is not
readable from the shell) shows YouTube and Netflix as KEY_UNKNOWN in `getevent -lt`, with MSC_SCAN
000c0077 and 000c0078: the usages the Google TV Streamer list maps to BUTTON_3 (190) and
BUTTON_4 (191).
- Home by redirect: launcherx and setupwraith left enabled for casting, stock_home_redirect set to
com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx, HomeKeyService enabled by hand. launcher/build-and-install.sh
with STOCK_LAUNCHER=none installs, then stops at its Home check, as expected while launcherx is
Home. Home pressed in an app landed on the new launcher. After a reboot the TV stayed on the Google
TV home: it is drawn before Android binds HomeKeyService, so no window change reaches the redirect
(#698 and #1024 work on this). With launcherx kept as Home, tools/check.py needs it as the second
argument, or every run reports Home as drift: the Check line in debloat-keep-cast.txt, which is the
list this setup matches.
- With the redirect on, the YouTube button did nothing although launcherx was enabled. The redirect
opens the launcher with ACTION_MAIN + CATEGORY_HOME, so this is consistent with #698's explanation
(this launcher becomes the Home process and launcherx loses its Android 14 exemption for background
activity starts, BAL_BLOCK), but no BAL_BLOCK line was captured in logcat. app_keys
"190:com.google.android.youtube.tv" and "191:<package>" in a theme, handled by HomeKeyService,
worked with both buttons on the real remote. (Seen on a build with a local boot check added to
HomeKeyService; the redirect's intent was main's.)
- Holding Volume Up on the real remote still ramped with HomeKeyService filtering keys (key_filter at
its default) and Button Mapper's accessibility service enabled as well. Not checked with
HomeKeyService alone.
Kept on purpose: Google Assistant (com.google.android.katniss), Cast receiver
(com.google.android.apps.mediashell), phone remote (com.google.android.tv.remote.service), Play Store /
Play Services, Gboard, Bluetooth, com.google.android.tv.dfuservice (remote firmware updates).
The receiver itself stays enabled, but casting still needs setupwraith for its credentials
(see the setupwraith quirks above).
Telemetry, feedback and ads

header: Google TV Streamer (2024, device kirkwood, model "Google TV Streamer" / GZRNL), 4 GB RAM
Google TV 14 (SDK 34), build UTTK.260317.003
Apply:   TV_HOST=<ip> tools/disable.sh examples/google-tv-streamer-4k-kirkwood/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<ip> tools/restore.sh examples/google-tv-streamer-4k-kirkwood/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.
This is a dongle: no Live TV app and no HDMI inputs, so leave live_tv_package empty in config.xml.
Known quirks on this firmware:
- ADB on port 5555 is closed (connection refused) until you pair once through Wireless debugging with
the stock adb: Developer options > Wireless debugging > Pair device with pairing code, `adb pair
<ip:pairport> <code>`, `adb connect <ip:connectport>` (`adb mdns services` lists both ports), then
`adb tcpip 5555`. After that tools/tv.py works on 5555
(docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md, "USB debugging never opens port 5555").
- The Cast receiver (com.google.android.apps.mediashell) reads its factory device credentials from a
provider hosted INSIDE the setup wizard package:
Provider{com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith/com.google.android.libraries.tv.setupwraith.libs.castinfo.CastInfoProvider}
There is no separate com.google.android.tvsetup package; the com.google.android.tvsetup.* classes
ship inside the setupwraith APK. Disabling setupwraith therefore takes the credentials out of
scope and casting dies with "No private key, hence empty signature" (docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md,
"Casting fails with Untrusted device"). This is NOT limited to Google's own Chromecast hardware:
it reproduces on the Google TV Streamer too (#361).
- The credentials only live in the receiver PROCESS. Re-enabling setupwraith and waiting for
"Created singleton instance of ClientAuthSigner" in logcat (about 7 s here) brings them back, but
`am force-stop com.google.android.apps.mediashell` loses them again ("Retry loading factory
credentials"), so the ritual has to be redone whenever the receiver is restarted.
- The manifest android:priority does NOT work on this build. Giving the replacement launcher
android:priority="3" on its HOME intent-filter was tried, the attribute IS in the installed APK
(aapt2 shows android:priority=3) and the PackageManager still reports priority 0, even after a
reboot. `cmd package set-home-activity` returns Success and does not change the dispatch either,
and the HOME role holder is ignored. The HOME can only be taken by DISABLING setupwraith
(package level).
- pm hide is not an alternative: `pm hide com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith` fails with
"SecurityException: Neither user 2000 nor current process has android.permission.MANAGE_USERS".
- Consequence for the Cast: with setupwraith disabled the receiver keeps the credentials in MEMORY
only, so after every reboot (or every receiver restart) the Cast has to be restored by briefly
re-enabling setupwraith and waiting for the signer:
logcat -c
pm enable --user 0 com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith
# wait ~30 s, then check logcat -d -s cast_shell for "Created singleton instance of ClientAuthSigner"
pm disable-user --user 0 com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith
Do not press HOME while setupwraith is enabled: RecoveryActivity may claim it (see below).
- If setupwraith is enabled and it wins HOME, RecoveryActivity runs as a DETACHED root task and
the first home transition kills the system, roughly every 47 s:
FATAL EXCEPTION IN SYSTEM PROCESS: android.display
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: positionChildAt:
container=Task=20383 is not a child of container=Task=1 current parent=null
at com.android.server.wm.WindowContainer.positionChildAt(WindowContainer.java:903)
at com.android.server.wm.Task.moveToBack(Task.java:4768)
at com.android.server.wm.TransitionController.tryStartCollectFromQueue
followed by DeadSystemException in setupwraith and com.android.systemui. The way out is to
disable the whole package, not the component:
pm disable-user --user 0 com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith
(`pm disable-user com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith/.RecoveryActivity` is refused with a
SecurityException, same as the stock launcher.)
- The saved Wi-Fi network belongs to the setup wizard on this device, so disabling setupwraith can
drop the device off Wi-Fi: `dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'`. tools/disable.sh skips
setupwraith when it sees that. Re-join the network from Settings > Network afterwards, and check
again: the network then belongs to android.uid.system:1000 instead.
If the guard skips setupwraith, re-join the Wi-Fi FIRST (so the network belongs to
android.uid.system:1000) and re-run, or force it with FORCE_SETUPWRAITH=1. On Ethernet the risk of
losing connectivity is nil, but the guard is about the saved network, not about the live link.
- With launcherx disabled the YouTube button on the remote does nothing. It sends BUTTON_3
(keycode 190). The launcher maps it itself: set app_keys to "190:com.google.android.youtube.tv"
in config.xml (or a theme's config.json) and enable InputKeyService:
settings put secure enabled_accessibility_services com.gathin.tvhome/.InputKeyService
settings put secure accessibility_enabled 1
Record the trigger with the physical remote: keys injected with `input keyevent 190` don't reach
the accessibility service. Key Mapper (keymapperorg/KeyMapper) does the same job if you prefer it;
the Play Store lists it as incompatible with this device, so install the -foss APK from its
GitHub releases, then over ADB:
pm grant io.github.sds100.keymapper android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS
settings put secure enabled_accessibility_services io.github.sds100.keymapper/io.github.sds100.keymapper.system.accessibility.MyAccessibilityService
Map trigger "Button 3" (short press) to action "Launch app > YouTube".
- The other two app buttons go silent with launcherx too. The remote's layout file
(/system/usr/keylayout/Vendor_18d1_Product_9451.kl, named by `dumpsys input`) maps them by HID usage:
usage 0x000c0077 -> BUTTON_3 (190)  YouTube
usage 0x000c0078 -> BUTTON_4 (191)  Netflix
usage 0x000c0186 -> MACRO_1  (313)  Star (launcherx opens the Google Home panel with it)
so app_keys "191:com.netflix.ninja" and "313:<package>" bring them back, with InputKeyService on.
`getevent -lt` prints the Star button as KEY_SPREADSHEET and the other two as KEY_UNKNOWN, which is
why the layout file is the place to read them. All three checked with the real remote on
- Both helpers cost the remote's key auto-repeat on this build: with HomeKeyService or InputKeyService
bound, holding Volume Up/Down stops after about six steps. The YouTube button can also be taken
without an accessibility service, which keeps the ramp: a shell-owned process watches the remote's
input device ("Google TV Remote Keyboard", found by name with `getevent -pl`, never by a fixed
number) and starts the app itself. It cannot consume the press, so the button's own action still runs
as well - see docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md, "Remapping the remote's app buttons without a key helper"
A second unit (same build, 2026-10-28) kept the YouTube button and the ramp together without a script, the
Sony VU3 way from that same TROUBLESHOOTING section: launcherx re-enabled after the install
(`pm enable com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx`), the theme's config.json setting
"stock_home_redirect": "com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx" and "key_filter": false, and HomeKeyService
enabled. YouTube then goes to launcherx's GlobalKeyListener_Receiver as stock, Home flashes launcherx and
lands on this launcher, and held volume ramps. It survived a reboot; the price is launcherx running again.
setupwraith stays disabled, so this does not bring casting back.
- com.google.android.tvrecommendations and com.google.android.apps.education.cast2class ship
disabled at the factory; `pm disable-user` on them fails with "Shell cannot change component
state". Don't add them to a restore list either.
- Disabling dreamx leaves screensaver_components pointing at it. Point it at the launcher's clock:
settings put secure screensaver_components com.gathin.tvhome/.ClockDream
- Animation scales already ship at 0.5x on this build.
Kept on purpose: Google Assistant (com.google.android.katniss), Cast receiver
(com.google.android.apps.mediashell), phone remote (com.google.android.tv.remote.service), Play Store /
Play Services, Gboard, Bluetooth, com.google.android.tv.dfuservice and
com.google.android.tv.overlay.dfuservice (remote firmware updates). The setup wizard
(com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith) is disabled, but the Cast credentials it hosts are restored
with the enable/wait/disable ritual described above.

Tested for one evening so far (Home, grid, D-pad, dock apps) and across one reboot: the disabled list and the

Notes from this box:
- The stock home is com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx. launcher/build-and-install.sh disables it.
- setupwraith's RecoveryActivity (HOME priority 1, launcherx 2, a sideloaded launcher 0) takes Home once
launcherx is off, so setupwraith has to go too, and it has to go FIRST. Redone in that order (setupwraith,
then launcherx), Home went straight to the new launcher. This is the same crash-loop xiaomi-tv-a-pro-2026
describes. Re-enable setupwraith to re-pair the remote.
- Disabling setupwraith takes the box off Wi-Fi in either order if the network was saved during first setup:
that network belongs to setupwraith, and Android deletes it with the app. The first run here most likely lost
Wi-Fi this way; the redo stayed online because the network had been re-joined by hand in between. Seen on a
second box (V816.0.7.0.UZFAABX): disabling setupwraith alone, launcherx still Home, logged
"WifiConfigManager: Remove all networks for app ... setupwraith" and dropped Wi-Fi and ADB within a second.
The network re-joined in Settings is a new entry owned by android.uid.system and survived disabling
launcherx and dreamx. Check before disabling: tools/tv.py "dumpsys wifi" | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'
- Leave alone: com.xiaomi.android.tvsetup.partnercustomizer, mitv.service, com.droidlogic*.
- With the stock launcher gone, apps without a dock slot just appear in the grid.
A second unit, same firmware (V816.0.11.0.UZFAABX), one evening and one reboot, applied this list with
YouTube Music, Assistant, Chromecast, Miracast/Mi share and the updater kept, plus the Privacy Sandbox group below:
- setupwraith owned no saved network here (every cname= was android.uid.system), so Wi-Fi and ADB stayed up.
- After the reboot, `pm list packages -d` matched what was disabled: the firmware re-enabled nothing.
- Wireless debugging leaves port 5555 open across reboots: switch off USB/Wireless debugging when done.
- Remote (Vendor_2717_Product_32b9.kl): once launcherx is off, Netflix (BUTTON_6) still opens Netflix, but
YouTube (BUTTON_3, scan 425), Prime Video (BUTTON_7, scan 207), Xiaomi TV+ (BUTTON_5, scan 150) and Apps
(ALL_APPS, scan 216) do nothing. config.json in this folder maps them back with app_keys, which needs
INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1 when running build-and-install.sh. The real Home button worked without HOME_KEY_SERVICE.
- The volume buttons send IR to the TV: `getevent -lt` shows no event on the box while they are held, so a held
button not repeating is the TV's doing, with or without a key helper.
- Remote shortcut keys (Vendor_2717_Product_32b9.kl): YouTube sends BUTTON_3 (scancode 425), Prime Video sends
BUTTON_7 (scancode 207), and Apps button sends ALL_APPS (scancode 216). Enable HomeKeyService
